clue.text: Bird to smoke at home

parts.note: to puff is to draw on a cigarette or pipe
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a bird might enjoy a quiet cigarette indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird with a striking colourful beak, a species of auk.

clue.text: More than one local in front of Borstal during discharge

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: pus is the discharge from an infected wound

indicators.note: the front of the word Borstal is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A young offender visiting pubs while on discharge from a youth prison.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's regular neighbourhood pub; Borstal was a British youth detention centre.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage your local is the nearby pub you frequent, so several of them are pubs.

clue.text: Following green light turning, hit red light at the back

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: turning means the word for the go-ahead is read backwards

parts.note: a green light is a go-ahead, permission to GO
to lamp someone is British slang for hitting them

explanation.surface: A driver moves off as the light changes to green and hits a car's rear light.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamp is British slang for punching someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's rear fog lamp is a bright red light at the back used in poor visibility.

clue.text: Not able to go one mile to receive inspection for vehicle

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word mile receives the test's abbreviation inside it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A car that cannot go another mile until it has passed its roadworthiness test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety check, named after the old Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Immotile is a biological term for something incapable of moving by itself.

clue.text: Crimes by receivers of stolen goods

parts.note: of can mean by, as in a work of or by an author
a fence is a dealer in stolen property

explanation.surface: A statement listing the crimes committed by people who handle stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are breaches of the law, a near synonym for crimes.

clue.text: In favour of Europe, ultimately still time for planning

parts.note: for means in favour of, as opposed to against

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Europe

parts.note: though can mean still or nevertheless

explanation.surface: A politician who supports Europe but still wants time for planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Forethought is careful consideration of the future, the essence of advance preparation.

clue.text: Venice trips to see show

indicators.note: trips suggests stumbling, so the letters of the city name fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An advert inviting holidaymakers on trips to Venice to see a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to reveal or display it plainly.

clue.text: Axe policeman for smuggling heroin

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden within, so the drug letter goes inside

parts.note: copper is informal British for a police officer
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A call to sack a police officer caught smuggling heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopper is a short-handled axe or cleaver used for chopping.

clue.text: One hanging poster about product's unmatched quality

indicators.note: about means the sender word goes around the marketing abbreviation

parts.note: a poster is one who posts something, a sender
USP is a unique selling point, what makes a product stand out

explanation.surface: An advertising poster about a product's special qualities is hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a strap from which a stocking hangs, so it is one that does the hanging.

clue.text: Couple that are not straight about male's forbidden love

indicators.note: about means the two words go around the letter for male

parts.note: bi and gay are two words for people who are not heterosexual
M is the abbreviation for male; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A same-sex couple caught up in a man's illicit love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy, marrying while already wed, is a love relationship banned by law.

clue.text: Characteristics describing Romeo meeting love rats

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the characteristics enclose the pair

parts.note: traits are distinguishing characteristics

indicators.note: meeting puts the two letters side by side

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo's traits, meeting his love, are those of a love rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats in slang are informers or people who betray their friends.

clue.text: PC? Priti Patel's flapping around when interviewed, for example

indicators.note: flapping suggests things thrown about in a panic, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the surname taken as written; the 's stands for is, a link
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Former Home Secretary Priti Patel flustered and flailing when quizzed by the media.
explanation.walkthrough: Priti Patel was the UK Home Secretary when this was published.
explanation.definitionFit: Interviewed is the past participle form of the verb to interview, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Actor tried playing king for role in theatre?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and reordered

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (rex)

explanation.surface: An actor tried playing a king, seeking a role in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An art director is the person overseeing visual design, a job in theatre and film.

clue.text: See people, not initially for sex

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like 'see', its common text-speak use

indicators.note: not initially means dropping the word's first letter

parts.note: the population is the people of a place

explanation.surface: An invitation to see people, though not for sex at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Copulation is the act of sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Like top kisser? Charlie excited on one date, finally has fiddle

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
up can mean excited or worked up
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word has

parts.note: to bow is to play a fiddle with a bow

explanation.surface: Charlie, excited on a first date, finally gets to fiddle about.
explanation.walkthrough: Kisser is slang for the mouth, so the top kisser is the upper lip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid's bow is the double curve of the upper lip, the shape of the top of the mouth.

clue.text: Made money on the radio

indicators.note: words heard on the radio are spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone who earned a fortune broadcasting on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means produced or reared, as in raising livestock, so it can mean made.

clue.text: Legendary figure to go brown: Greek character around lake getting sun

parts.note: to tan is to go brown in the sun

indicators.note: around means the Greek letter goes about the lake abbreviation

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A Greek man tanning around a lake in the sun, like a mythological figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantalus is the Greek myth's king punished with food and water forever just out of reach.

clue.text: Poke with end of sharp stick

indicators.note: the end of the word sharp is its final letter

parts.note: a rod is a stick or pole

explanation.surface: Poking something with the pointed end of a sharp stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to jab or poke with a finger or pointed object.

clue.text: Hide round bike sheds, primarily to smoke

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: to cure fish or meat is to preserve it, for example by smoking

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren hiding round the bike sheds, mainly to have a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind the bike sheds is the stereotypical British school spot for illicit smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it or make it hard to see.

clue.text: Top worker to call teacher

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: An office boss needs to phone a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Top here means the big top, the circus tent, not a senior employee.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster presents the acts in a circus, working under the big top.

clue.text: One holds guy, perhaps, after ten pints knocked back

indicators.note: after means the example abbreviation comes behind the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: knocked back means the abbreviation is turned around

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for pint
EG, for example, can stand for perhaps

explanation.surface: A man perhaps holding himself up after downing ten pints.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is a guy rope, the cord that steadies a tent; 'perhaps' is wordplay, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg is driven into the ground to anchor the rope pulled taut from a tent.

clue.text: Crumbled in golf on series of holes

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a round of golf is a series of holes played

explanation.surface: A golfer crumbled under pressure during a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground is the past tense of grind, so ground coffee is crushed into small particles.

clue.text: Disintegration after treatment is confusing

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked on and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient's state falling apart after medical treatment is bewildering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disorientating causes loss of one's bearings, leaving one bewildered.

clue.text: Aware of boozer drinking round

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the pub word swallows the round letter

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A pub where someone is drinking a round.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in on something is to share knowledge of a secret or plan.

clue.text: What for Don Juan stops fights? Bunches of flowers

indicators.note: stops means plugging a gap, so the Spanish word goes inside

parts.note: bouts are boxing or wrestling fights
que is Spanish for what, as the Spanish lover Don Juan would say

explanation.surface: A legendary womaniser asks how to stop fights, and is handed flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouquets are arranged bunches of flowers given as gifts.

clue.text: Polish almost off new shoe

indicators.note: off suggests going bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word falls short of its last letter

explanation.surface: Nearly all the polish has worn off a new shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-on is a shoe without laces that is simply slid onto the foot.

clue.text: They hold Women's Institute meeting with more senior people

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
elders are people older than oneself

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute branch meeting its most senior members.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a long-established British organisation, often associated with jam and Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Wielders are people who hold and use tools or weapons, such as a sword.

clue.text: Regular shape in keeping very fit

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word in holds the other two

parts.note: taken as written
so means very, as in so tired
go can mean fit, as in this key won't go in the lock

explanation.surface: A routine for staying in good physical shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An isogon is a polygon with all its angles equal, a regular geometric figure.
